title: How a retaining wall holds up a hill
caption: Why backyard walls don't just fall over 🧱⛰️ #howitsbuilt #retainingwall #landscaping #construction #howitworks

lines.text: If you just stacked blocks against a hill, the first big rain would push the whole wall over.
So you dig a trench and pack it with gravel, so the wall has a solid base.
But blocks sitting on the ground can slide right out at the bottom.
So you bury the first row, and the dirt holds its feet in place.
But a wall standing straight up still tips forward.
So each row sits a little behind the one below, and the wall leans into the hill.
But rain soaks the soil behind it, and that water can double the push on the wall.
So you fill the space behind the blocks with *gravel*, which lets the water drain straight down.
And a *drain pipe* full of holes at the bottom carries it away.
But mud washes into the gravel and clogs it.
So you line it with *filter fabric*, which lets water through but holds the dirt back.
But a taller wall gets shoved by a huge mass of dirt.
So you lay plastic mesh called *geogrid* between the rows, reaching back into the hill, so the soil and wall act like one big block.
Then glue cap stones on top.
Congratulations, you just built a *retaining wall*.
